name: West Ridge

waypoints.name: Phelps Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR-207 north, turn right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then left onto Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200). Follow it about 22 miles, the last half on rough dirt, then turn right at the signed Phelps Creek turnoff and climb FR 6211 about 2 miles to the Phelps Creek Trailhead at the road end (about 3,500 ft). High clearance helps on these roads.

pitch_detail.notes: Ascend scree/talus gully from upper Phelps Basin (~5,700-6,000 ft) toward Dumbell's south ridge and the connecting col.
Long, narrow, exposed ledge on Dumbell's east face; roughly a foot wide in spots, passes under a small overhang requiring a crawl in one section; snow-covered into mid-August.
From the ~7,900 ft notch on the southeast ridge (last 100 ft to the notch is loose Class 2+), walk up talus and scree on the West Ridge to the summit.

beta: From a camp in upper Phelps Basin, climb scree/talus below Dumbell's south side to a long, narrow, airy ledge that wraps around Dumbell's east face to the Dumbell-Greenwood col near a 7,900 ft notch on Greenwood's southeast ridge (the final 100 ft to the notch is loose Class 2+). From the notch/col, an easy Class 2 talus walk up the West Ridge leads to the summit, which has a summit register (kept in a Boy Scouts of America can on the south summit). The route is unroped scrambling throughout, but the connecting ledge is in places only about a foot wide with steep exposure, passes under a small overhang requiring a crawl in one spot, and can hold snow and require an ice axe/crampons into mid-August.
descent_text: Descend the West Ridge talus back to the ~7,900 ft notch, then carefully reverse the narrow connecting ledge around Dumbell's east face to the col above the south-side gully. Downclimb the loose Class 2-3 gully/ledges back into upper Phelps Basin; on snow, plunge-stepping or glissading speeds this section when conditions allow. There is no rappel route commonly described for this line — the ledge and gullies are downclimbed. Do not attempt the ledge crossing in the wet; several parties have retreated rather than cross it in rain.
